faqs.q: Are timber rattlesnakes really around Crestview?
faqs.a: Yes — the timber (canebrake) rattlesnake occurs in the Panhandle's pine woods and river swamps, including Okaloosa's northern country, though it is shy, uncommon near houses, and protected by no special status but deserving of distance. Copperheads are the more likely venomous encounter in leaf-littered hammock edges. Keep woodpiles and brush away from the house, watch footing in the swamp fringe, and photograph unknowns from distance. A confirmed rattlesnake taking residence by a home is a specialist removal; a ratsnake in the woodpile is pest control with scales.

faqs.q: An alligator lives in Rocky Bayou near our Niceville dock — problem or neighbor?
faqs.a: Usually a neighbor. Choctawhatchee Bay's bayous are alligator habitat, and a gator that keeps its distance and is under four feet is part of the scenery FWC generally leaves be. The thresholds for FWC's nuisance program are size — four feet or more — plus threatening behavior toward people, pets, or property. Never feed it, keep dogs out of the bayou at dawn and dusk, and report bold behavior. No private company may remove an alligator; that work belongs solely to FWC's contracted program trappers.
